title: A 5% drainage-shape bound shows a sample-dependent post-1997 change in south-east Australian dry spells
abstract: We test unforced positive linear-store mixtures with dry-day flow triplets in CAMELS-AUS v2.03. Such mixtures require convex log flow. For a declining triplet that fails this condition, we derive the exact smallest maximum relative correction to a valid exponential. In 238 south-east Australian catchments, the matched event share above a 5% correction bound rose from 6.49% in 1951-1996 to 8.50% in 1997-2021. The change was 2.01 percentage points, with a joint 95% time and space interval of 0.32 to 3.67 points. SILO rain gave a similar broad result. Later-period and strict-rain tests had intervals across zero. With final flow at least 0.1 mm/day, 62-66 catchments had no clear increase. These catchments also had no increase without the flow floor. Thus the broad change depends on the sample and does not establish a persistent regional change in drainage physics. The 5% level is an assumed error tolerance, not a measured gauge error. The test cannot separate delayed recharge, nonlinear drainage, loss or data error, and does not close the annual water budget. Code, source hashes, aggregate estimates, all joint draws, proofs and audits are supplied. External daily and event records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: An exact flow correction bound and historical changes in event shares above a 5% bound. Intervals jointly sample five-year time blocks and spatial cells. The higher-flow subset has no clear increase.
